title: Hydraulic performance of 14-G hemodialysis catheters versus an 8-Fr arterial cannula in a mock 3-kg small-dog cardiopulmonary bypass circuit
content:
by Keizo Wauchi, Chisato Ikubo, Hirohito Imada, Masahiro Miyata, Kenji Tani

Arterial cannulation for cardiopulmonary bypass in small dogs is challenging because small vessel diameters may preclude use of appropriately sized pediatric arterial cannulas. Although off-label use of 14-gauge hemodialysis catheters has been reported, their pressure–flow characteristics under small-dog cardiopulmonary bypass conditions remain unclear. This in vitro study evaluated one 8-French pediatric arterial cannula and six 14-gauge hemodialysis catheter specimens—separate side-hole and sealed specimens at effective lengths of 25, 32, and 38 mm—in a closed-loop mock circuit for a 3-kg small dog. A 34% (w/w) glycerol–water solution (viscosity 2.8 cP at 28°C) served as an approximate Newtonian blood analogue. The Stockert S5 pump flow-rate setting was increased from 50 to 350 mL/min; 50–300 mL/min was prespecified as the primary analysis range and 350 mL/min as exploratory. The reported outlet pressure was recorded 1,000 mm upstream of the test device, while inlet pressure was monitored 300 mm downstream and regulated to 60 mmHg; six technical runs per condition were conducted using the same physical device and circuit setup. Within the primary analysis range, outlet pressure was approximately 136–137 mmHg at 300 mL/min; mean differences for the 14-G specimens versus the 8-French cannula were +0.33 to +0.67 mmHg, with 95% confidence intervals from −1.33 to +2.15 mmHg. At 350 mL/min, outlet pressures were higher for all three side-hole 14-gauge specimens than for the 8-French cannula. At 300 mL/min, outlet pressure was approximately 2–3 mmHg lower for the side-hole specimens than for the sealed specimens across all catheter lengths. Together, these findings indicate small observed circuit-level differences in outlet pressure among tested devices within this standardized mock small-dog cardiopulmonary bypass circuit, but do not establish formal equivalence, device-to-device interchangeability, or clinical validity.
